composition_parti.rule: The facade is near-symmetrical, not strict-bilateral: openings are located by the rooms behind them and then nudged toward apparent balance, so exact symmetry is a frequent outcome rather than a governing rule.
composition_parti.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited strict-bilateral-odd-bay (via colonial-revival's own family, eclectic-revivals), which is the wrong composition mode for this node: the style's own governing_logic states plainly 'nothing is derived from a module of order' and that apparent rhythm is a residual of plan-driven openings, not a designed symmetry system.

variants.note: The FHA's most-published elevation and Levitt's chosen form (cape-cod-massing, canonical massing affinity).
Named directly in defining_characteristics: 'gabled or hipped.'
The single-storey version with a projecting entry or living-room gable, the one compositional move the style allows itself (massing_affinities, common).
Overrides the cascade's inherited value (shingle-style, via colonial-revival's family). No source names a gambrel roof for this node; the roof is a simple gable or hip throughout.

roof_form.rule: Compact rectangular or shallow-L massing under a simple gable or hip roof, one storey or one and a half. No secondary roof form of any complexity.
roof_form.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 1-2. Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'gambrel' from shingle-style (spliced in via colonial-revival's own family, eclectic-revivals), which contradicts this node's own stated roof forms.

roof_pitch.rule: Roof pitch 4:12 to 6:12 -- a hard constraint (c02) and a repeated figure in typical_ratios.
roof_pitch.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'pitch_min=9:12' from queen-anne-american (spliced in via colonial-revival's own family), which is nearly double this node's own documented ceiling and directly contradicts its own hard constraint c02.

roof_material.rule: Low-fired clay barrel tile (the cascade's inherited value from mediterranean-vernacular, spliced in via a distant family branch) has no basis anywhere in this node's own text or lineage and is climatically and economically wrong for an FHA production house of the 1930s-1950s in climate zones 2-6.
roof_material.note: Forbidding only, not specifying a replacement: the node's own text never names a roofing material directly, so asserting one (asphalt composition shingle is the well-known historical answer) would be an unsourced positive claim. Marked judgment because the forbidding itself is inferred from context (region, era, cost-engineering) rather than from an explicit statement.

eave_condition.rule: Eave and rake overhang not exceeding 12 in and frequently under 6 in, closed tight to the wall plane with no bracket, rafter tail, or purlin end -- 'a recognizably traditional shape with essentially no eave... the roof surface stops at the wall surface and the two meet without a shadow line' (diagnostic_tells).
eave_condition.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited shingle-style's eave rule verbatim (spliced in via colonial-revival's own family), which happens to share the same 12 in ceiling by coincidence but is sourced from an unrelated style and omits this node's own, far more diagnostic point -- that the overhang is frequently zero and the wall meets the sky with no shadow at all.

gable_treatment.rule: A single small gabled or hipped entry projection or bay is permitted as the only three-dimensional event on the whole elevation; anything more is outside the node.

variants.note: A later, non-original expansion of the attic on one-and-a-half storey examples, not part of the style's original vocabulary.

dormer.rule: Dormers are not part of the original design vocabulary; where one appears on a one-and-a-half storey example it is a shed dormer added at the rear in a later remodel, not an original feature.

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (georgian-colonial-american, via colonial-revival's family). A door this elaborate contradicts the node's own description of a budget-permitting 'simple door surround' at most.

entry_door.rule: The door itself carries no ornament beyond, at most, a simple applied surround if the budget allowed; it sits in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less and no projecting surround.
entry_door.note: Direct quote of the long description ('a simple door surround') and diagnostic_tells item 3. Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved six-panel raised-and-fielded door is Georgian-Colonial-American's own high-style door, wholly inconsistent with this node's cost-engineered minimalism.

door_surround.rule: No projecting classical surround of any kind. The door lies in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less; a pilasters-and-entablature treatment (the cascade's inherited value) is exactly the kind of expensive, cost-engineered-out element this style deleted first.
door_surround.note: Direct quote of diagnostic_tells item 3 ('the front door lies in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less and no projecting surround'). Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved pilasters-and-entablature surround is inherited from english-georgian/colonial-revival via the family splice and directly contradicts this diagnostic.

variants.note: This node's own, actually-built answer: 'a detached garage at the rear of the lot, reached by a driveway beside the house' (distinguished_from vs ranch-style). Retrieved from documented practice, not invented -- Minimal Traditional predates the attached-garage problem the rest of the family exists to solve.

Where the type is reproduced on a modern infill lot without room for a detached rear garage, the family's own 4 ft-setback / 33-percent-width answer (mid-century-traditional.garage_strategy) applies. This half of the entry is an editorial extension for contemporary buildability, not a historical fact about the 1930s-50s house.

garage_strategy.rule: The type's own historical answer to the garage predates the problem the rest of the family exists to solve: keep it detached at the rear of the lot. A contemporary reproduction on a lot too narrow for that reverts to the family's later, invented answer.

edit_provenance.note: The canonical variant is retrieved directly from the node's own text, not invented -- unlike ranch-style and neo-eclectic, Minimal Traditional's garage is a solved problem by its own account. The permitted contemporary-infill variant is an honest editorial addition, flagged as such rather than presented as period fact.

porch_type.rule: No full- or partial-width habitable porch (hard constraint c04, soft severity on the entry-cover-projection number). Entry is a stoop, at most under a small hood or shallow entry gable, with cover projection not more than 3 ft.
porch_type.note: Direct quote of minimal-traditional.c04 and defining_characteristics item 3.

steps_and_stoop.rule: Entry is a plain stoop, occasionally under a small hood; there is nowhere to stand out of the rain beyond it.
steps_and_stoop.note: Direct quote of the long description's own summary of the style's felt experience ('there is nowhere to stand out of the rain').

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (english-georgian, via colonial-revival's family). This node's whole point is the absence of a classical-depth trim system.

trim_family.rule: Trim of minimal profile depth: flat frieze board, narrow clamshell or ranch casing (2 1/4 in wide, under 3/4 in projection -- see the already-specified `casing` slot), and no cornice return of any consequence.
trim_family.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 5. Fixes a cascade bug: english-georgian's real, deep classical trim system (gibbsian-bolection) is inherited via the family splice and is precisely what this style deleted.

circulation_parti.rule: A cellular plan of small, individually-walled rooms rather than an open or flowing plan; circulation is not itself a compositional device.
circulation_parti.note: Direct quote of distinguished_from[ranch-style] ('Minimal Traditional is an upright compact block with a cellular plan'). Marked judgment because the node's own text names the plan type in passing, in a comparison to another node, rather than describing it directly as its own subject.
